page: Microsoft Azure D32ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C x86_64 processor with 16 physical cores and 32 dedicated vCPUs operating at 4.2 GHz. The processor features a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per vCPU.

This server includes 1890 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and supports Premium Storage. In benchmark testing, the D32ds_v6 demonstrates strong performance in static web serving throughput at 56.21 GB/sec and text processing. It also exhibits top-tier performance in small-model LLM text generation, achieving 355.44 tokens/sec for a 135M model, alongside strong prompt processing speeds. However, memory performance shows some limitations, with a weak Passmark memory score of 1699.64, and large-block memory write bandwidth is measured at 55.49 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D32ds_v6 offers a balanced resource density, combining dedicated high-frequency compute cores with a substantial local NVMe SSD allocation. This makes it highly suitable for workloads that require a mix of CPU power and fast local scratch space without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. Appropriate workloads include database operations, static web serving, software compilation, and light-to-medium LLM inference tasks.
